The claim states that for each sample point P, the signed distance d_i is calculated as F(P) for all active planes. Source [S1] explicitly defines the signed distance function F(x,y,z) and states: 'From this we can compute a signed distance to that plane for any given 3D coordinate (x,y,z).' It further explains that clipping involves determining if points are inside or outside based on this signed distance. Therefore, the evidence supports the claim that the signed distance is computed for sample points relative to the planes.
